contribution: Microeconometric methods for panel data and their use to study household behavior, labor supply, consumption and inequality
rationale: Recent prizes covered institutions (2024) and innovation-led growth (2025), so the committee may turn to empirical microeconomics and econometrics. Blundell is a perennial frontrunner for his work on labor supply, consumption, inequality and tax policy. Arellano's dynamic panel-data methods, including Arellano-Bond, are among the most-cited tools in economics. The two share a coherent theme of household dynamics and panel econometrics. This is a guess under high uncertainty; Fehr, Blanchard and Saez are also strong possibilities.
